# Kubernetes

A [Continuous Compliance Framework](https://compliance-framework.github.io/docs/) plugin that collects Kubernetes resources and evaluates OPA/Rego policies against them.

Supports multiple authentication methods (EKS via AWS STS, kubeconfig for any cluster) and concurrent multi-cluster collection.

> **Breaking change in this release.** The plugin now implements the `RunnerV2` interface and evaluates policies **per individual resource** rather than per cluster. The Rego input schema has moved from `v1` (`input.clusters[...]`) to `v2` (`input.main` + `input.context`). Existing policies that read `input.clusters[...]` must be rewritten. Companion policy repos (`plugin-k8s-policies`, `plugin-k8s-opres-policies`) will be updated in a coordinated follow-up.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-k8s` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.2.4](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-k8s/releases/tag/v0.2.4) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.2.4](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-k8s/blob/v0.2.4/README.md).

## Configuration

### Plugin Configuration

The plugin receives configuration as flat string fields from the CCF agent. All structured values are JSON-encoded strings.

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `clusters` | Yes | JSON array of cluster connection configs |
| `resources` | Yes | JSON array of Kubernetes resource types to collect (e.g. `"nodes"`, `"pods"`, `"deployments"`) |
| `main_resources` | No | JSON array — subset of `resources` that produces per-instance subjects and evidence. Defaults to all of `resources`. Types in `resources` but not in `main_resources` are collected as policy context only. |
| `identity_labels` | No | JSON object mapping identity-label key → ordered list of `metadata.labels` keys to try. Default: `{"app_name": ["app.kubernetes.io/name", "app"]}`. First match wins; falls back to `metadata.name` when none are present. |
| `namespace_include` | No | JSON array of namespaces to include (empty = all) |
| `namespace_exclude` | No | JSON array of namespaces to exclude |
| `policy_labels` | No | JSON object of key-value labels added to evidence metadata |
| `policy_input` | No | JSON object of custom fields merged into the Rego input document. Reserved keys: `schema_version`, `source`, `main`, `context`, `subject`, `fleet`. |

#### Cluster Configuration

Each entry in `clusters` has:

| Field | Required | Provider | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | all | Unique display name for this cluster |
| `provider` | No | all | `"eks"` (default) or `"kubeconfig"` |
| `region` | Yes | eks | AWS region |
| `cluster_name` | Yes | eks | EKS cluster name |
| `role_arn` | No | eks | IAM role ARN to assume before authenticating |
| `kubeconfig` | No | kubeconfig | Path to kubeconfig file (default: `~/.kube/config`) |
| `context` | No | kubeconfig | Kubeconfig context to use (default: current-context) |

### Configuration Examples

#### Single EKS cluster — evidence per pod, nodes as context

```json
{
  "clusters": "[{\"name\":\"prod\",\"region\":\"us-east-1\",\"cluster_name\":\"prod-eks\"}]",
  "resources": "[\"nodes\",\"pods\"]",
  "main_resources": "[\"pods\"]",
  "namespace_exclude": "[\"kube-system\",\"kube-public\"]",
  "policy_labels": "{\"team\":\"platform\",\"environment\":\"production\"}",
  "policy_input": "{\"expected_azs\":[\"us-east-1a\",\"us-east-1b\",\"us-east-1c\"]}"
}
```

#### Custom identity label

```json
{
  "clusters": "[{\"name\":\"prod\",\"region\":\"us-east-1\",\"cluster_name\":\"prod-eks\"}]",
  "resources": "[\"pods\"]",
  "identity_labels": "{\"app_name\":[\"app.company.io/service\",\"app.kubernetes.io/name\"],\"team\":[\"team.company.io/owner\"]}"
}
```

#### EKS with cross-account role assumption

```json
{
  "clusters": "[{\"name\":\"prod\",\"region\":\"us-east-1\",\"cluster_name\":\"prod-eks\",\"role_arn\":\"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-readonly\"}]",
  "resources": "[\"nodes\",\"pods\"]",
  "policy_input": "{\"expected_azs\":[\"us-east-1a\",\"us-east-1b\"]}"
}
```

#### Local cluster via kubeconfig (kind, minikube, k3s)

```json
{
  "clusters": "[{\"name\":\"local-dev\",\"provider\":\"kubeconfig\"}]",
  "resources": "[\"pods\",\"services\",\"deployments\"]",
  "namespace_include": "[\"default\",\"app\"]"
}
```

#### Multi-cluster (mixed providers)

```json
{
  "clusters": "[{\"name\":\"prod-east\",\"region\":\"us-east-1\",\"cluster_name\":\"prod-east-eks\"},{\"name\":\"prod-west\",\"region\":\"us-west-2\",\"cluster_name\":\"prod-west-eks\"},{\"name\":\"dev\",\"provider\":\"kubeconfig\",\"context\":\"kind-dev\"}]",
  "resources": "[\"nodes\",\"pods\"]",
  "main_resources": "[\"pods\"]",
  "namespace_exclude": "[\"kube-system\"]",
  "policy_input": "{\"expected_azs\":[\"us-east-1a\",\"us-east-1b\",\"us-west-2a\",\"us-west-2b\"]}"
}
```

## Evidence collected

### Subjects and evidence model

During `Init`, the plugin registers one `SubjectTemplate` per entry in `main_resources` (e.g. `k8s-pods`, `k8s-nodes`). Each template has the identity label keys:

- `cluster_name`
- `namespace` (only for namespaced resources)
- `app_name` (resolved from `metadata.labels` via `identity_labels`; falls back to `metadata.name`)
- `name`

For cluster-scoped resources such as `nodes`, the emitted evidence labels still include `namespace` with an empty string so label contracts stay stable, but the corresponding `SubjectTemplate` omits `namespace` from its identity keys and rendering.

During `Eval`, every concrete Kubernetes resource instance that matches a `main_resources` type becomes its own subject and receives its own evidence for every configured policy path. Policies are invoked once per `(resource instance, policy path)` pair. Evidence is batched per cluster, and a batch is sent with `CreateEvidence` when it reaches 100 evidences or when the policy-evaluation data it holds reaches a byte limit, whichever comes first.

Each evidence carries a JSON copy of the Rego input it was evaluated against, and that input includes every collected resource in the fleet (`input.context` and `input.fleet`). With large clusters a single input can be tens of MiB, so the byte limit is what keeps memory bounded.

#### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CCF_K8S_EVIDENCE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` | `67108864` (64 MiB) | Maximum total size, in bytes, of the policy-evaluation input and policy data held in one evidence batch. Lower it if the plugin runs out of memory. Invalid or non-positive values fall back to the default with a warning. |

The agent passes its environment through to plugin processes, so set this on the agent.

## Policy input

The plugin implements input schema `v2` only: a policy runs once per resource instance and policy path, and receives one document as `input` with the resource under evaluation in `input.main` and the whole cluster snapshot in `input.context`. There is no `input.clusters`, the shape of schema `v1`. Only resource types listed in `main_resources` (all of `resources` when it is not set) are evaluated; the others are collected and appear in `input.context.resources` and `input.fleet` as context only. Fields are listed by their path inside the document. Resources are the unstructured objects the Kubernetes API returns, so only their top level is described here; the keys of `input.context.resources` are the resource names from the `resources` setting in lower case. A field marked as left out is missing from the document, not null. A policy sees the data of the cluster being evaluated in `input.context`, and the data of every cluster in `input.fleet`. Every evidence carries a JSON copy of this input, which includes every collected resource, so the document can be large. Your own policy data from the agent configuration is in `data.<key>`, not in `input`. Custom fields from the `policy_input` setting are merged into the top level of the document. That setting is a JSON object, and the plugin refuses to start when it holds one of the reserved keys `schema_version`, `source`, `main`, `subject`, `context` or `fleet`, so a custom field can never replace what the plugin sets.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | string | Always `v2`. |
| `source` | string | Always `plugin-kubernetes`. |
| `main` | object | The Kubernetes resource under evaluation, as the API returns it (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`, `status` and the rest). |
| `subject` | object | Identity of the resource under evaluation. The fields below are inside it. |
| `subject.cluster_name` | string | Name of the cluster, the `name` set for it in `clusters`. |
| `subject.resource_type` | string | Resource type, as listed in `main_resources`, such as `pods`. |
| `subject.name` | string | The resource's `metadata.name`. |
| `subject.namespace` | string | The resource's `metadata.namespace`. Left out for cluster-scoped resources. |
| `subject.identifier` | string | Stable identifier of the resource's subject, `k8s-<resource type>/<cluster>/[<namespace>/]<app name>/<name>`, each part lower case with characters other than letters, digits and `-` replaced. |
| `subject.identity_labels` | object (string to string) | One entry per key of `identity_labels` (`app_name` by default). The value is the first of the key's `metadata.labels` that the resource has, looked up in the resource's labels, its pod template labels and its selector `matchLabels`; the resource's `metadata.name` when none match. |
| `context` | object | The cluster the resource belongs to, with its snapshot. |
| `context.cluster` | object | Cluster the resource belongs to, with `name`, `region` and `provider` (`eks` or `kubeconfig`). `region` is empty for a `kubeconfig` cluster that has none. |
| `context.resources` | object (string to array of objects) | Every collected resource of this cluster, keyed by resource type. Includes the resource in `main` and the types that are in `resources` only. |
| `fleet` | object | Snapshot of all clusters collected in this run. |
| `fleet.clusters` | object | Keyed by cluster name. Each entry has `cluster` (the same `name`, `region` and `provider` object as `context.cluster`) and `resources` (the same map as `context.resources`). |
| `<custom key>` | any | A field you set in the `policy_input` setting, merged at the top level. Not a reserved key. |

An example input:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "v2",
  "source": "plugin-kubernetes",
  "main": {
    "apiVersion": "v1",
    "kind": "Pod",
    "metadata": {
      "name": "web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde",
      "namespace": "shop",
      "uid": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
      "labels": {
        "app.kubernetes.io/name": "web"
      }
    },
    "spec": {
      "nodeName": "ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal",
      "containers": [
        {
          "name": "web",
          "image": "registry.example.com/shop/web:1.4.2"
        }
      ]
    },
    "status": {
      "phase": "Running"
    }
  },
  "subject": {
    "cluster_name": "prod",
    "resource_type": "pods",
    "name": "web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde",
    "namespace": "shop",
    "identifier": "k8s-pods/prod/shop/web/web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde",
    "identity_labels": {
      "app_name": "web"
    }
  },
  "context": {
    "cluster": {
      "name": "prod",
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "provider": "eks"
    },
    "resources": {
      "nodes": [
        {
          "apiVersion": "v1",
          "kind": "Node",
          "metadata": {
            "name": "ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal"
          }
        }
      ],
      "pods": [
        {
          "apiVersion": "v1",
          "kind": "Pod",
          "metadata": {
            "name": "web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde",
            "namespace": "shop"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "fleet": {
    "clusters": {
      "prod": {
        "cluster": {
          "name": "prod",
          "region": "us-east-1",
          "provider": "eks"
        },
        "resources": {
          "nodes": [
            {
              "apiVersion": "v1",
              "kind": "Node",
              "metadata": {
                "name": "ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal"
              }
            }
          ],
          "pods": [
            {
              "apiVersion": "v1",
              "kind": "Pod",
              "metadata": {
                "name": "web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde",
                "namespace": "shop"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "expected_azs": [
    "us-east-1a",
    "us-east-1b"
  ]
}
```

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### k8s-pods

One template for each type in `main_resources` (all of `resources` when it is not set), registered when the agent calls `Init`; the name is `k8s-` and the resource type in lower case, so `main_resources` of `["pods", "nodes"]` registers `k8s-pods` and `k8s-nodes`. The first example is for a namespaced type, `pods`. Every template is a component with the same identity keys, a title of `Kubernetes <type> [<namespace>/]<name> in <cluster_name>`, a description of `Kubernetes <type> <name> in cluster <cluster_name>[ under namespace <namespace>]` and the purpose `Individual Kubernetes <type> instance evaluated by the Kubernetes plugin.` The namespace part is left out of the title and description when the namespace is empty. Evidence also carries `resource_type` and the labels from `policy_labels`, which are not part of the identity. Each evidence is also linked to a cluster component, `k8s-cluster/<cluster name>`.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `cluster_name` | Name of the cluster the resource belongs to. |
| `namespace` | Namespace of the resource. An empty string for cluster-scoped resources such as nodes. |
| `app_name` | Application name, resolved through `identity_labels`. When you add keys to `identity_labels`, their values go in evidence labels but the template's identity keys stay these four. |
| `name` | The resource's `metadata.name`. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "k8s-pods",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "Kubernetes pods shop/web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde in prod",
  "description": "Kubernetes pods web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde in cluster prod under namespace shop",
  "purpose": "Individual Kubernetes pods instance evaluated by the Kubernetes plugin.",
  "identityLabels": {
    "cluster_name": "prod",
    "namespace": "shop",
    "app_name": "web",
    "name": "web-7d9f8c6b5-abcde"
  }
}
```

### k8s-nodes

The same template for a cluster-scoped type, here `nodes`. The namespace is empty, so the evidence label `namespace` is an empty string and the title and description leave the namespace out.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `cluster_name` | Name of the cluster the node belongs to. |
| `namespace` | Always an empty string for nodes. |
| `app_name` | Falls back to the node's name, since nodes rarely carry an application label. |
| `name` | The node's `metadata.name`. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "k8s-nodes",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "Kubernetes nodes ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal in prod",
  "description": "Kubernetes nodes ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal in cluster prod",
  "purpose": "Individual Kubernetes nodes instance evaluated by the Kubernetes plugin.",
  "identityLabels": {
    "cluster_name": "prod",
    "namespace": "",
    "app_name": "ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal",
    "name": "ip-10-0-1-23.example.internal"
  }
}
```

## Policies

The policy bundles that work with this plugin, at their newest releases. The controls are the ones the bundle's policies list in their metadata.

| Bundle | Latest version | Controls covered | Compatible plugin lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`plugin-k8s-opres-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-k8s-opres-policies) | `v0.2.1` | *none listed* | latest |

### Policy data

Any `policy_data` set on this plugin's block in the agent configuration is passed
to every policy evaluation and is available to Rego as `data.<key>` (unlike
`policy_input`, which is merged into `input`):

```yaml
plugins:
  kubernetes:
    # ...source, policies and config as usual...
    policy_data:
      allowed_registries:
        - ghcr.io/compliance-framework
```

### Example: writing a policy

```rego
package compliance_framework.pod_has_node_binding

import rego.v1

violation contains {"remarks": msg} if {
    input.main.kind == "Pod"
    not input.main.spec.nodeName
    msg := sprintf("Pod %q has no nodeName assigned", [input.main.metadata.name])
}

# Cross-reference sibling resources via input.context
violation contains {"remarks": msg} if {
    input.main.kind == "Pod"
    node_name := input.main.spec.nodeName
    not node_exists(node_name)
    msg := sprintf("Pod %q binds to unknown node %q", [input.main.metadata.name, node_name])
}

node_exists(name) if {
    some n in input.context.resources.nodes
    n.metadata.name == name
}

title := "Pod node binding"
description := "Every pod must bind to a known node in its cluster."
```

Key patterns:
- `input.main` is always the single resource under evaluation.
- `input.context.resources.<type>` is the full cluster snapshot; iterate with `some r in ...`.
- `input.context.cluster` gives the cluster name/region/provider for labels and messaging.
- Filter out the main resource from peer checks with `r.metadata.uid != input.main.metadata.uid`.
